author: Phillip Inman
description:
Bank of England expected to keep rates on hold on Thursday but renewed Iran conflict casts shadow over energy costs

The Bank of England could be forced to tear up its economic forecasts and raise interest rates later this year if oil prices return to above $100 a barrel, according to City economists.

Before a meeting of Bank officials on Thursday, economists said that while an interest rate hike would probably be avoided this week there could be some in the future because of conflict in the Middle East.

Continue reading...
title: Rising oil prices could force up UK interest rates, say economists

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Figures are source of dispute as US defense department days ago reduced record of troops killed and wounded

The Pentagon updated its official war casualty database over the weekend, adding more than 140 wounded service members. The Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) also introduced a new casualty category labeled “Overseas Operations” for personnel killed and wounded “starting July 7”.

According to the updated database, the official toll for the earlier phase of the US-Iran war, known as Operation Epic Fury, now stands at 14 service members killed and more than 400 wounded in action.

Continue reading...
title: Pentagon reports more than 600 Iran war casualties in quiet database update

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Minister says Victorian premier ‘not going anywhere’ and describes leaking of Sunday night meeting as attempt to build momentum for spill

The Victorian Labor premier, Jacinta Allan, is expected to face a leadership challenge when state parliament resumes this week.

Just four months out from a state election, factional conveners from Labor’s left and right met on Sunday night to discuss whether Allan still had the support of a majority of the caucus. It is understood the group agreed she did not.

Continue reading...
title: Jacinta Allan expected to face leadership challenge after Labor factions meet

author: Stephanie Convery
description:
New tidal baths on banks of Callan Park in Lilyfield expected to attract thousands to Parramatta River’s southern banks. Follow the day’s news

Morning folks, Stephanie Convery with you here to bring you all the live news today. Thanks so much to my colleagues for kicking us off this morning.

Cam McEvoy has dominated the 50m freestyle final in Glasgow, breaking the Commonwealth Games record, AAP reports.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: new Sydney Harbour pool slated to open in summer; AusAlert warning test to blare siren across phones nationally

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Scott Gottlieb responds to report that company contacted the White House seeking to delay a recall announcement

Former Food and Drug Administration commissioner Dr Scott Gottlieb said on Sunday that it was “not standard operating procedure” for Taylor Farms to ask the White House to intervene as the company prepared to announce a recall tied to a massive cyclospora outbreak.

Appearing on CBS’s Face the Nation, Gottlieb was asked about a report from the Wall Street Journal that Taylor Farms contacted the White House seeking to delay a recall announcement while federal investigators were preparing to publicly link the company to the multi-state outbreak.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Not standard’ for Taylor Farms to ask White House to delay cyclospora recall, ex-FDA head says

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Singer rebukes Trump administration after it uses her song Firework over footage of missile striking Iranian naval ship

Pop star Katy Perry has condemned the Trump White House after it used her hit song Firework in a TikTok video showing US military strikes on Iranian targets, saying she never approved the use of her music.

The White House video, which featured Firework playing over footage of a missile striking an Iranian naval ship, has amassed more than 6 million views. The post was captioned: “Iran has been warned.”

Continue reading...
title: Katy Perry ‘deeply appalled’ over White House using her song in Iran war video

author: Maya Yang
description:
New law prohibits retailers from using personal data to charge different prices for identical products

New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill recently signed a new law prohibiting businesses from using shoppers’ personal information to charge different prices for identical products, making her state the third in the US to ban the practice.

The Fair Price Protection Act passed by New Jersey’s legislature seeks to protect consumers from surveillance pricing, in which retailers can use data including online activity, location and purchasing history to arbitrarily change prices for individual shoppers.

Continue reading...
title: New Jersey governor signs law banning surveillance pricing to protect shoppers

author: Penry Buckley and Krishani Dhanji
description:
Christian Ellis, a former registered lobbyist, is named in two Independent Commission Against Corruption allegations

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A key figure at the centre of an anti-corruption inquiry involving the New South Wales Liberal party has moved to the UK and is not expected to give evidence during eight weeks of public hearings.

The Independent Commission Against Corruption will start its Operation R
title: Former NSW Liberal powerbroker at heart of Icac allegations now living in UK and not expected to appear

author: Josh Butler
description:
Exclusive: Malcolm Roberts uses white supremacist concept to describe the party’s plans for deporting 200,000 people from Australia

Senator Malcolm Roberts claims One Nation wants to deport at least 200,000 people and has repeatedly referred to the far-right concept of “remigration” in podcast interviews and speeches to niche platforms.

In two recent podcasts, Roberts said One Nation wanted to deport 100,000 temporary residents as well as 100,000 international students – a total much higher than the party’s published policy. The senator said after those people were removed, he wanted to “start working on the higher numbers of people we need to get rid of”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Get rid of them’: One Nation senator claims party will ‘remigrate’ illegal visa holders in resurfaced interview

author: Ben Doherty
description:
Exclusive: Tribunal accepts three siblings could face ‘persecution’ for refusing military conscription due to their political opinion on war

Three Israeli citizens facing conscription into the Israel Defense Forces have been granted the right to reapply for protection visas in Australia, after a government tribunal found they held a genuine fear they would be forced to break international humanitarian law in Gaza.

The Administrative Review Tribunal found the punishment the young adults could face from the state of Israel – including imprisonment as conscientious objectors – would amount to persecution.

Continue reading...
title: Israeli siblings who fear breaking law in Gaza under IDF owed protection by Australia, tribunal finds

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Union calls for museum to become accredited London living wage employer and let staff carry water during shifts

Workers at one of the world’s leading art and design museums are balloting for “heatwave” strike action.

The ballot at V&A is taking place because of concerns about soaring temperatures and access to drinking water, along with pay and conditions.

Continue reading...
title: V&A workers hold ballot to strike over pay and heatwave conditions

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Sara Gilson was fatally shot less than two weeks after accusing her husband of pedophilia on social media

An Oklahoma woman known for posting on social media about parenting her children was fatally shot in an apparent murder-suicide by her husband a short time after she published a clip alluding to allegations that he had molested a minor, according to authorities and court records.

Sara Duffey – who was 43 and also went by Sara Gilson – Jeremiah Shawn Duffey, 48, were both found dead with gunshot wounds on Thursday at a home in suburban Tulsa, said statements from local police. Investigators suspected that Jeremiah had shot Sara and then himself.

Continue reading...
title: Oklahoma influencer killed in apparent murder-suicide by husband, police say

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Airport’s bars and restaurants also unable to serve drinks to passengers because of lack of running water

A water supply failure at Gatwick has left passengers without access to working toilets or bars and restaurants.

Passengers posted online that they were unable to get hot drinks, wash their hands or fill up water bottles at the airport in Sussex.

Continue reading...
title: Water supply failure leaves Gatwick without working toilets

author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris, Sam Jones in Madrid and Jennifer Rankin
description:
Efforts to contain wildfire that has consumed an area of four times the size of Paris impeded by windy conditions

  • Europe wildfires live – latest updates

Authorities are battling to contain a huge wildfire near Bordeaux in south-west France that has consumed an area of land four times the size of Paris.

Efforts to extinguish the blaze in the Gironde region, where nearly 220,000 people have been evacuated, were hampered by windy conditions on Saturday night.

Continue reading...
title: Firefighters in France battle to prevent huge blaze from approaching Bordeaux

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Experts say evidence for cognitive screening desired by health secretary ‘not great’ as taskforce idle since last year

The US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, has called for better Alzheimer’s screening – but a critical federal panel that might have helped researchers find practical ways to do that has been prevented from meeting for more than a year.

The panel, formally called the US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF), had planned to issue a recommendation on screening for cognitive decline this year, alongside 13 other topics as varied as autism screening and food allergy prevention.

Continue reading...
title: RFK Jr urges Alzheimer’s screening but blunts key panel that could drive research

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
PM promises to ‘defend national interest before anything else’ in first big broadcast interview since entering No 10

Andy Burnham has promised to disagree with Donald Trump if necessary, including in public, in his first big broadcast interview since becoming prime minister.

Burnham’s comments came as Wes Streeting, the new defence secretary, said he did not believe the Trump administration was looking for allies who “suck up”, but rather those with the confidence to set out disagreements when needed.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham says he will disagree with Trump in public if necessary

author: Rob Davies
description:
England’s progress provides best football-related uplift of recent years, with one pub too packed to host its Dolly Parton tribute

Late opening hours and England’s progress to the semi-final of an expanded World Cup helped provide the best football-related uplift of recent years for pubs, figures suggest.

Pubs poured 30m extra pints over the course of the tournament compared with a normal trading period, with busy pumps delivering £150m in added sales, according to the British Beer & Pubs Association (BBPA).

Continue reading...
title: ‘Weekday games were amazing’: pubs toast extra £150m in World Cup sales

author: Caitlin Cassidy(earlier)
description:
This blog is now closed

‘We’re cohesive’: PM says after muted ALP national conference

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, spoke with David Speers on Insiders as Labor’s 50th national conference in Adelaide was wrapping up.

Well, our government does listen to people but [there was a] broad consensus about the direction in which we’re taking government … A government that doesn’t sit idle. We don’t just occupy the space. And there’s recognition of that from delegates that we are a united party We’re cohesive.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Socialist’ teachers target eight Victorian Labor MPs including education minister – as it happened

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Campaigners say existing federal ban on phone or video calls for assisted dying consultations adversely affects people living in regional Australia

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor will come under pressure to implement changes to its national policy platform and allow Australians to access voluntary assisted dying through telehealth services, with the Greens and independent Kate Chaney to introduce legislation.

title: Labor under pressure to allow telehealth access for euthanasia but PM says ‘it should be face-to-face’
